summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, a history of kidney and pancreas transplants, atrial fibrillation, and multiple comorbidities was admitted due to an elevated INR of 9.8. She had recently undergone peritoneal dialysis catheter placement and had stopped warfarin, but her INR continued to rise. She also reported symptoms of esophagitis, likely candidal, and was started on fluconazole. Her INR improved to 4.6 with vitamin K administration. Medication adjustments included holding warfarin, starting fluconazole, and planning reductions in tacrolimus and sirolimus due to drug interactions. She remained stable, her PD catheter site was healing, and she was discharged back to extended care with instructions for close monitoring of INR and immunosuppressant levels.
